boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented Florida Atlantic rituals, recurring events, and spirit objects—from a four-story pumpkin drop to the brass bell rung after home victories.

cards.title: Keep the Cord from Day One
cards.subtitle: Freshman Convocation begins and eventually bookends the FAU journey
cards.notes: Attend your designated ceremony, bring an Owl Card or Event Pass, and keep the blue-and-silver cord safe to wear at commencement.
cards.short_summary: Incoming Owls receive a graduation cord years before they graduate.
cards.evidence_claim: FAU describes Freshman Convocation as the official beginning of a student’s college career and says attendees receive a blue-and-silver cord to wear at commencement.
cards.access_notes: Only attending freshmen receive the cord; students must attend their designated ceremony and bring an Owl Card or Owl Central Event Pass.

cards.title: Welcome Football with Fire
cards.subtitle: FAU’s annual fall kickoff burns bright before football season
cards.notes: Watch the university’s official event schedule, then join the crowd from designated viewing areas and follow all on-site safety directions.
cards.short_summary: Music, smoke, and Owl cheers signal the approach of football season.
cards.evidence_claim: FAU identifies the annual fall bonfire as a university tradition sponsored by the Student Government Program Board with university partners to celebrate the start of football season.
cards.access_notes: Attend only the officially scheduled university event and remain within designated spectator areas; current date and entry details require confirmation.

cards.title: Listen for Sixty Pounds of Victory
cards.subtitle: A solid-brass bell announces FAU home wins
cards.notes: After an Owl home victory, listen for the bell rather than approaching event equipment or entering any restricted game-day area.
cards.short_summary: A substantial brass bell turns every home-team win into a campus sound.
cards.evidence_claim: FAU says the 60-plus-pound solid-brass Taylor Victory Bell rings after every home win by an FAU team and was donated by Robert and Nina Taylor in 2010.
cards.access_notes: The ringing is tied to FAU home wins; attending the associated athletic event may require a ticket or credential.

cards.title: Meet at the Rat’s Mouth
cards.subtitle: FAU’s oddly named fan gathering occupies Lot 5
cards.notes: Meet fellow fans in Lot 5 before a home game, keep celebrations under-21-safe, and observe posted parking and stadium rules.
cards.short_summary: Boca Raton’s translated name becomes an unmistakably FAU rallying point.
cards.evidence_claim: FAU calls the Rat’s Mouth its legendary tailgating spot and states that the fan gathering is located in Lot 5 on the north side of the stadium.
cards.access_notes: Located in Lot 5 north of FAU Stadium; confirm current game-day parking, tailgating, and stadium policies before visiting.

cards.title: Build a Human Tunnel for the Team
cards.subtitle: Students and spirit squads create FAU football’s entrance lane
cards.notes: Check the football schedule, arrive before team entry, and stand only where game-day staff direct students and supporters to gather.
cards.short_summary: The Owls enter through a corridor made from their own campus community.
cards.evidence_claim: FAU documents Owl Walk as a football tradition in which students, the Marching Owls, and Cheer and Dance Teams form a human tunnel for the team’s stadium entrance.
cards.access_notes: This football game-day activity occurs near the student tailgate area; timing, participation rules, and ticket requirements should be confirmed.

cards.title: Rub Owlsley’s Beak for Luck
cards.subtitle: An exam-day superstition lives outside the recreation center
cards.notes: Stop at the Owlsley statue before an exam or competition, gently rub the beak, and leave space for others taking photographs.
cards.short_summary: FAU luck is sought from the polished beak of a class-gift mascot statue.
cards.evidence_claim: FAU says students often rub the beak of the Owlsley statue for luck before exams and competitive events; the statue was a gift from the Classes of 2008 through 2011.
cards.access_notes: The statue stands outside the Recreation and Fitness Center; outdoor access may be affected by campus operations or nearby events.

cards.title: Let Faculty Serve Finals Breakfast
cards.subtitle: Late-night meals turn FAU staff into student waiters
cards.notes: As finals approach, check the campus event listing and bring any requested student identification before joining the late-night breakfast.
cards.short_summary: Finals stress pauses while faculty and staff serve a free evening meal.
cards.evidence_claim: FAU says free Night Breakfasts are presented on its Boca Raton and Jupiter campuses near finals, with music and entertainment and faculty and staff serving as waiters.
cards.access_notes: Held late at night as finals approach; verify the current campus, date, time, venue, eligibility, and check-in requirements before attending.

cards.entity_name: The Pumpkin Drop and Physics Carnival
cards.title: Study Physics by Dropping Pumpkins
cards.subtitle: FAU professors turn a four-story fall into a science lesson
cards.notes: Watch from the marked spectator zone, listen for the costumed scientists’ explanations, and stay for the physics-themed carnival games.
cards.short_summary: Smashed pumpkins become a theatrical demonstration of fundamental physics.
cards.evidence_claim: FAU documents an annual fall Pumpkin Drop in which professors drop pumpkins from the roof of the Schmidt College of Science building, followed by a Physics Carnival.
cards.access_notes: This recurring fall demonstration requires spectators to use designated viewing areas; verify the current date, location, and public-access details.

cards.title: Wear FAU Colors Every Tuesday
cards.subtitle: Tuesday spirit gear can unlock limited-edition campus swag
cards.notes: Wear FAU gear on a fall or spring Tuesday, then look for Program Board’s tent on Diversity Way while supplies remain.
cards.short_summary: FAU turns an ordinary weekday into a recurring red-and-blue dress ritual.
cards.evidence_claim: FAU describes BLUEsday as a weekly fall-and-spring tradition in which people wearing FAU gear can visit the Program Board tent on Diversity Way for free swag.
cards.access_notes: Runs on Tuesdays during fall and spring semesters; giveaways are limited to the first eligible visitors and current tent details should be confirmed.

cards.title: Strike the Coach’s Sideline Pose
cards.subtitle: Fans mirror FAU football’s founding coach inside Stadium Gate 1
cards.notes: On an FAU Stadium visit, find the statue just inside Gate 1 and recreate Schnellenberger’s pose without blocking pedestrian flow.
cards.short_summary: A stadium photograph imitates the stance of the coach who built Owl football.
cards.evidence_claim: FAU invites fans to pose with the Howard Schnellenberger statue, which depicts the founding football coach’s iconic pose and stands just inside Gate 1 at FAU Stadium.
cards.access_notes: The statue is inside Gate 1 at FAU Stadium, so access may depend on stadium openings, event admission, and security procedures.
